item.turbines.pearlescent_dew_bucket.too: A hyper-energetic alchemical fluid that burns at extreme temperatures. Only Steam Boilers have the refractory capacity to contain its heat so most engines would melt down instantly.
Burns at heat level 4.0, exceeding superheated limits. Consumes very slowly. Only compatible with the Steam Boiler and incompatible with other engines and blaze burners.
block.turbines.steam_boiler.tooltip.summ: Produces Steam which can be fed to Steam Turbines, Steam Pumps, Steam Compressors, and Pressurized Steam Pipes. Make sure to feed it fuel and water!
block.turbines.steam_boiler.tooltip.beha: It can consume liquid fuels too. Pearlescent Dew is the best fuel source for the Steam Boiler. Feed water and liquid fuel through pipes or from buckets, and supply solid fuels with mechanical arms.

Recommended layout: place a Steam Pump directly after the boiler, a Steam Compressor after the pump, then Steam Turbines afterwards, further down the line. Place Pressurized Pipes between the boiler and pump if you want to combine multiple boilers into a unit/cluster.
block.turbines.pressure_pipe.tooltip.sum: Holds Steam for other machines. Use it along with a Pressurized Steam Pump to move steam between machines together.
block.turbines.pressure_pipe.tooltip.beh: The pipes do not move steam on their own. Use a Steam Pump to move steam through them.
Uses rotational force supplied on the sides to compress Steam to have higher pressure and throughput. Place it after either a Steam Pump.
Pressure and throughput scale with the rotational RPM, and the kinetic stress impact obviously increases the higher the RPM goes.
Outputs to any other machine that accepts steam input, like the Steam Turbine and Steam Jet Thruster.
block.turbines.steam_turbine.tooltip.sum: Consumes Steam to generate power which is sent to the Steam Turbine Shaft. You can chain 10 of these together for higher SU.
block.turbines.steam_turbine.tooltip.beh: More pressure and throughput = more power produced and more turbines you can chain. Steam weakens as it moves between turbines, so 10 chained turbines is the max before the Steam Turbine Shaft.
You can view the stats of these with engineer goggles.
block.turbines.turbine_shaft.tooltip.sum: Generates SU from chained Steam Turbines.
block.turbines.turbine_shaft.tooltip.beh: The turbine shaft calculates turbine count, pressure, and throughput for the total SU output. Increasing these = more SU.
Steam is exhausted on the side too!
block.turbines.steam_pump.tooltip.summar: Pulls steam from all connected Pressurized Steam Pipes and machines that output steam into one direction.
block.turbines.steam_pump.tooltip.behavi: The Pump has an adjustable Pump Rate. Increasing this also increases the Kinetic Stress Impact, and higher RPM increases the Stress Impact as well.
Pump Rate and RPM control steam transfer speed. Higher values transfer steam faster.
block.turbines.steam_jet_thruster.toolti: Consumes Steam to produce directed thrust. Connect a compressor along with a pump for increased efficiency and power.
block.turbines.steam_ejector.tooltip.sum: Consumes Steam to pump fluids up to 80 blocks away at 10 pressure and 3 Steam/t. Lower pressure or throughput reduces range, but transfer speed stays at 1 bucket per second.
block.turbines.large_turbine.tooltip.sum: A horizontal rotor stage designed for Hydro Turbine chambers with 1 to 10 vertical stages.
block.turbines.lava_duct_turbine.tooltip: Generates SU based on how many sides are touching lava. Each side touching lava produces 475 SU. Place below a Lava Duct Shaft and stack multiple turbines up to 5 max.
block.turbines.lava_duct_shaft.tooltip.s: Collects SU from Lava Duct Turbines placed below it. Outputs kinetic power and requires continuous water supply to its copper pipe side.
block.turbines.directional_analog_gearsh: A directional gearshift controlled by analog redstone signals. The LEFT and RIGHT sides determine output speed and direction from their signal differential.
Output speed follows the input direction with an RPM modifier based on the redstone differential. Higher differential = higher speed.
Output direction is locked to an absolute direction determined by which redstone side is stronger. The input direction is completely ignored; only the speed magnitude is used.
Kinetic input must be supplied from the BACK side (Marked Red). The OPPOSITE side (Marked Blue) is the output.
block.turbines.network_diagnoser.tooltip: Displays network RPM, SU usage, and allows stress testing. Right-click to configure.
Shows live RPM and stress data from the connected kinetic network when viewed with engineer goggles.
When active, injects configurable stress into the network to test capacity limits.
